title: Generation of Shear Adhesion Map Using SynVivo Synthetic Microvascular Networks
protocol: Submerge the SynVivo-SMN microfluidic device in sterile deionized (DI) water.
Place Tygon tubing primed with water into each port of the device using fine-point forceps.
Remove air from the channels of the device by running a vacuum for approximately 15 minutes.
Insert Tygon tubing approximately 1 inch long into each port after removing the device from water.
Prepare a drop of water (approximately 100 µl) around the base of one inlet port tubing.
Carefully remove the tubing used to prime the device, ensuring the water drop prevents air entry.
Prepare a 1 ml syringe loaded with avidin at a concentration of 20 µg/ml.
Connect the syringe to a stainless steel needle and tubing.
Insert the tubing into one of the inlet ports of the device.
Clamp the inlet port not being utilized with a jaw clamp.
Inject avidin at a flow rate of 1 μl/min for 10 min.
Clamp the tubing with the jaw clamp after injection.
Place the device at 4°C overnight.
Allow the device to come to room temperature.
Prepare a solution of 2 µm biotinylated particles at a concentration of 5 x 10^6 particles/ml in Phosphate Buffer Saline (PBS).
Load the biotinylated particle solution into a 1 ml syringe.
Prepare a second 1 ml syringe containing only PBS.
Load both syringes onto a syringe pump and connect them to needle and tubing.
Place a drop of water around the base of the inlet port tubing.
Insert the tubing for biotinylated particles and PBS into each of the inlet ports.
Start injecting biotinylated particles at a flow rate of 2.5 μl/min.
Monitor the inlet port on the microscope.
Begin timing when particles first appear in the inlet port.
Continue flow for 3 min after starting the timer.
Stop the flow of biotinylated particles and start the flow of PBS simultaneously.
Allow PBS to flow through the device at a rate of 2.5 μl/min for 3 min to wash off unbound particles.
Use the "scan large image" function to acquire an image of the entire device.
Sequentially number the bifurcations in the device.
Create a circular AOI with twice the diameter of the channels, setting the AOI diameter to 200 µm since the channel diameter is 100 µm.
Use the automated count function to export the number of particles in each AOI to an MS Excel sheet.
Use the automated count feature to export the number of particles in the entire device.
Run CFD simulations using commercially available software (CFD-ACE+, ESI Inc.) for the SynVivo-SMN device topology.
Store simulation results, including wall shear rates, velocity, particle flux, and adhesion information, in a database.
Use simulation results to determine the number of particles entering each AOI based on a given inlet particle concentration.
Calculate % of adhesion by dividing the adhered particles in the bifurcation by the particles flowing in the bifurcation.
